key_insight: Fourth-generation synchrotron imaging needs scintillators that are both faster and brighter than LYSO, and LaBr3/CeBr3 are strong near-term candidates for ultrafast X-ray diagnostics.
engineering_relevance: Improving scintillator speed, light output, and UV-sensitive readout is critical for enabling 13 MHz hard X-ray phase-contrast imaging and dynamic materials experiments at APS-U.
method: Characterized fast scintillator materials for decay time and light yield
Integrated scintillators into detector/optical packaging for ultrafast cameras
Tested performance in beamline experiments and compared emerging alternatives
evidence_signal: The abstract reports material characterization, detector integration, packaging, and beamline experiments showing LaBr3 and CeBr3 achieve about half the decay time of LYSO/LSO while maintaining comparable light yield.
watch_item: Many promising scintillators are hygroscopic and emit mainly below 400 nm, so packaging and high-quantum-efficiency UV readout remain major implementation challenges.
paper_title: Fast and bright scintillators for ultrafast materials dynamics using 4th generation synchrotron
